payload.title: tsk-4fx's batching fix (raceAcrossProcesses batchSize=4) is not enough: an independent reviewer…
payload.description: tsk-4fx's batching fix (raceAcrossProcesses batchSize=4) is not enough: an independent reviewer reproduces a real lock-timeout failure in test/state/store.test.mjs's concurrent-editWork-on-different-ids test (line ~840) and a real live-tee interleave failure in test/runner/loop.test.mjs's parallel-dispatch test (line ~1082), both with a consistent signature across repeated runs on their checkout. I could not reproduce either under synthetic CPU load alone (busy-loop stress up to load avg ~51 on 16 cores, and CPU-pinned 2-core contention) -- both suites stayed green. But this same shared dev machine is currently running with swap 100% full and ~1.2GB free RAM out of 15GB even at rest, which is a plausible real trigger: the events.lock budget in src/state/events.mjs (EVENTS_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000ms, untouched since tsk-4fx) is a fixed wall-clock window that can't tolerate real I/O stalls from swap thrashing, only CPU contention. Confirmed via git diff that neither failing test was touched by the unrelated tsk-40m work under review, so this is pre-existing standing fragility, not a new regression. Fix direction: tsk-4fx's own RESEARCH.md already named a second option it didn't take -- make the lock acquisition budget scale with observed contention (or make EVENTS_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS configurable/adaptive) instead of relying only on lowering peak concurrent contention via batching, since batching alone doesn't help when the slowdown is I/O-bound rather than CPU-bound.
